Devon: Quick question — partner asks to eval embeddings derived from support chat transcripts. We scrubbed direct names/emails but kept paraphrased context (issue descriptions, timeline). Are embeddings considered personal data if the raw text had PII removed?

Mina: Short answer: potentially. If embeddings are reversible or can be linked back to a person via metadata, treat as personal data. Also consider whether paraphrases preserve identifiable context. :thinking_face:

Devon: SG. Any guidance on concrete steps? We were planning to share an S3 bucket with vectors + message IDs (no user IDs).

Mina: Don't share message IDs if they map to internal logs. Options: 1) aggregate at conversation level, 2) apply irreversible hashing + salt and delete mapping, 3) run a k-anonymity filter on context. See internal doc: https://redwood.internal/policies/data-classification (section "Derived Data & Embeddings").

Raj: Quick follow-up — embeddings are numeric arrays; are they covered by our DP policy? Partner will run nearest-neighbor over the vectors.

Mina: If partner can probe and reconstruct or link, escalate. For NN workloads, add differential privacy or noise if it's user-sensitive. If it's low-sensitivity support categories, then removal of identifiers + sampled noise might be OK.

Ava: For timeline — partner needs data by EOD Friday. If we need DP/noise, that's not trivial. Can we provide a synthetic/aggregated test set instead?

Devon: Good call. We'll see if synthetic convo samples meet their eval. If not, we'll ask for a DPA + vendor SOC2 and a scoped access request.

Mina: Yes — require vendor controls (DPA + SOC2) and least-privilege access. File a vendor access request and add requirement: no reidentification attempts, and return or delete vectors on contract termination.

security-bot: Automated note: Please open a security request ticket for third-party data access: https://redwood.internal/sec-requests/new — include data classification and retention window. :lock:

Devon: Will open ticket now and flag product for timeline tradeoffs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
